query: What does the REJECT directive do in LeX when regular expressions conflict?
expected_answer: The REJECT directive selects the next alternative accepting action when regular expressions conflict, so all possible accepting actions for the input get executed.
expected_facts: selects the next alternative accepting action

relevant_passages.quote:
Add the REJECT directive to I.FX. This directive selects the next alternative 
accepting action when regular expressions conflict.

query: How do I turn off all the special start-condition expressions after activating a class with BEGIN?
expected_answer: Use BEGIN 0; to disable all special regular expressions.
expected_facts: BEGIN 0; disables all special regular expressions

relevant_passages.quote:
Use BEGIN 0; to disable all special 
regular expressions.

query: If users can change the regular expressions at installation time with a binary table file, how is the action for a modified expression chosen, and why must the number of expressions stay constant?
expected_answer: Actions are compiled into the program and cannot be read from disk at run time, so the number of expressions must stay the same. The position of a regular expression from the top of the file determines which action runs, so the second action runs for the second expression even if it was changed.
expected_facts: actions must be compiled into the program
cannot be read from disk at run time
position from top of file determines the action
number of expressions must stay the same

relevant_passages.quote:
Note that the actions still have to be put into the compiled program-there's no 
way to read them from disk at run time.

The position of the regular expression from the top of the file 
determines the action to execute when that expression is recognized.

query: Does wmove allow moving the cursor outside the window, and does it support negative coordinates for wrapping?
expected_answer: The document says wmove goes to a window-relative position and that you can't go outside the window, clamping coordinates with min() against the window size. It does not say anything about negative coordinates or wrapping.
